chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

He mentioned semen and treated it strictly, making it more severe than urine. Then he said: “If you see semen before, or after, entering into the salat, then you must repeat the salat. But if you examined your garment and did not find it, then prayed in it, and only afterward saw it, then there is no repetition upon you; and likewise with urine.”
So if najasah affects a person's garment, and he has no other clothes with him, he removes it and prays naked while seated; and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ الصَّلَاةِ: repeating the salat due to invalidation from impurity
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, a najis substance with a comparable ruling in this context
key_terms.الْمَنِيَّ: semen, treated here as a major impurity affecting the validity of salat
key_terms.ثَوْبِكَ: your garment, whose purity is a condition discussed here
key_terms.عُرْيَانًا: naked, meaning without the impure garment when no alternative clothing is available
key_terms.قُعُودٍ: sitting posture, the manner of praying indicated here in that circumstance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if semen or urine is found on one's clothes before or after salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on najasah affecting one's clothing during salat, especially concerning semen and urine. It distinguishes between discovered impurity that was previously checked for and impurity knowingly seen before or during prayer, and it also addresses praying without clothing when no pure garment is available.
